question: Where can I get a list of data centers in operation in the United States, with location, operator and capacity (IT power in MW or floor area)?

answer.summary: No unified U.S. federal registry of operating data centers exists. For free national structured data, start with FracTracker's U.S. Data Centers Tracker API (536 Operating sites with US coords, 353 operators, 423 MW/sq ft; non-commercial terms) and PNNL's IM3 Atlas GeoJSON (1,850 US centroids, 1,732 exterior sq ft, 1,199 operators, ODbL 1.0, no MW). Add Epoch AI (60 US operational AI sites with isolated IT MW, CC BY 4.0) and PeeringDB (1,381 US colocation facilities with operator/coords, no capacity). Authoritative official layers are localized (Loudoun GIS, VA DEQ, TX Comptroller). Paid Compute Atlas ($150/mo) and Cleanview ($4,900+) improve IT MW coverage.
main_caveats: Official data gap: U.S. federal agencies (DOE/LBNL, EIA, OMB) publish no public national facility inventory; DOE/LBNL's 2025 Update explicitly relies on proprietary market trackers (Omdia, IDC, S&P Global).

Capacity definition traps: FracTracker 'mw' reports total facility/build-out power demand rather than operational IT MW; IM3 'sqft' measures exterior OSM building/campus footprint, not interior IT floor space.

IT MW isolation: Among free sources, only Epoch AI (60 operational US frontier AI facilities) isolates IT power (MW) from total facility power; Compute Atlas ($150/mo) and Cleanview ($4,900+) cover broader IT MW.

License and completeness: FracTracker prohibits commercial use in its Terms of Service and undercounts smaller/older colocation facilities; PeeringDB covers 1,381 colocation sites but lacks MW/sq ft and private hyperscalers.

Sub-national fragmentation: Official county/state datasets cover high-density pockets (Loudoun GIS 187 built buildings with sq ft; VA DEQ 98 operating sites; TX Comptroller 182 tax-certified sites without coords/capacity).
answer.confidence_reason: Confirmed absence of a federal registry across DOE/LBNL, EIA, OMB, HIFLD, Census, and EPA; tested all national open APIs/downloads directly, validated US bounding boxes, and checked sub-national and commercial sources.

attributes.note: Free datasets provide verified US lat/lon and street addresses (FracTracker 536/536 coords, IM3 1,850 centroids, PeeringDB 1,358/1,381 coords, Epoch 57/60 addresses).
Filled for PeeringDB (1,381/1,381), Epoch (54/60), FracTracker Operating (353/536), IM3 (1,199/1,850), Loudoun parcels (131/139), and TX (182/182); undisclosed under NDAs.
attributes.gap_note: No national legal disclosure mandate exists; NDAs, holding-company LLCs (TX Comptroller/Loudoun parcels), and unmapped OSM features leave operator names blank on many facilities.

example.example_request: curl -sL "https://epoch.ai/data/data_centers/data_centers.zip" -o /tmp/ec3.zip && python3 -c "import zipfile,csv,io,json; z=zipfile.ZipFile('/tmp/ec3.zip'); r=[x for x in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(z.read('data_centers.csv').decode())) if x['Country']=='United States' and float(x.get('Current power (MW)') or 0)>0]; print(json.dumps({'us_operational':len(r),'sample':{k:r[0][k] for k in ['Name','Owner','Address','Current power (MW)']}}))" && rm -f /tmp/ec3.zip

local_terms.meaning: Electrical power delivered specifically to compute/server racks, excluding cooling and PUE overhead. Isolated in Epoch AI (free) and Compute Atlas / Cleanview (paid), unlike FracTracker gross facility MW.

Full substation or behind-the-meter electric load serving both IT and cooling systems (FracTracker 'mw', utility load requests); typically 1.15x-1.5x critical IT MW and often reported at full multi-phase build-out.

local_terms.term: White space vs. gross building sq ft
local_terms.meaning: Gross permitted building floor area (Loudoun GIS SQUARE_FEET) includes mechanical/power halls, whereas IM3/OSM 'sqft' measures exterior building or campus parcel polygon footprints rather than net raised-floor IT white space.
Texas Comptroller tax-exemption status requiring >=100,000 sq ft plus capital investment and job commitments; registration does not guarantee current online operation.
Georgia DCA regional planning filing for large proposed developments (including hyperscale data centers), reporting planned building square footage prior to construction.

Defunct OMB program (M-16-19 / M-19-19, ended Oct 2020) tracking federal government-owned data centers; ITDashboard.gov is sunsetting effective April 2026 and WhiteHouse/datacenters was archived in 2022.
